title: Day-2 provisioning & affinity constraints — terraform sketch for mixed on-prem clusters
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for Day-2 provisioning semantics and affinity/anti-affinity primitives when managing mixed on-prem Kubernetes clusters (vSphere + bare metal). Target audience: infra engineers and SREs who implement Terraform modules for node pools, rack-awareness, and upgrade orchestration.

Goals (high-level):
- Provide Terraform-first primitives to express rack/zone anti-affinity for workloads and nodes.
- Encode safe Day-2 operations: node additions, replacements, and rolling kernel/container-runtime upgrades.
- Minimize blast radius during upgrades by combining topology-aware placement + controlled drain windows.
- Support hybrid inventory (vSphere clusters + BMC-provisioned bare metal) under a single module surface.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers present metadata: physical_rack (string), hypervisor_cluster (vcenter name), and site_zone (A|B|C).
- vSphere VMs can be created with placement hints (host+datastore tags) but not strict anti-affinity across racks; use tags + placement policy.
- Bare metal nodes will be labeled with rack and BMC-facility attributes during provisioning.
- Network fabric may not support cross-rack multicast; we must assume higher pod startup latency across racks.

Module sketch (Terraform API surface) — variables and resources (informal):
- variables:
  - variable "cluster_id" { type = string }
  - variable "node_pools" { type = list(object({ name=string, count=number, flavor=string, topology=map(string) })) }
  - variable "topology_hints" { type = map(string) } # e.g., { "anti_affinity_level" = "rack" }
  - variable "maintenance_windows" { type = list(object({start=string,end=string,timezone=string})) }

- outputs:
  - node_pool_ids -> list of node ids (VM UUIDs / BMC asset ids)

- resources (abstract):
  - vsphere_vm (for vSphere-backed nodes) with a placement_tag derived from topology_hints (e.g., host-affinity-tag)
  - bmc_provision (for baremetal) which triggers PXE/IPMI workflow and attaches node labels for rack/site
  - k8s_node_registration module that applies node labels/taints via bootstrap token and cloud-init
  - topology_group resource (pseudo-resource) that maps node ids to topology buckets used by scheduling policies

Affinity and anti-affinity approach (runtime vs scheduler):
- Node labeling: always label nodes with: topology.kubernetes.io/region=<site>, topology.kubernetes.io/zone=<rack>, redwood/inventory-source=<vsphere|baremetal>
- Recommended scheduler policy: preferDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution for most workloads, with requiredDuringScheduling for critical control-plane components limited to masters.
- For stateful sets with replica>=3, enforce pod anti-affinity across topology.kubernetes.io/zone (rack). Use topologySpreadConstraints for best-effort distribution.
- Provide a helper module that generates both: KubernetesTopologySpreadConstraint and PodAntiAffinity snippets from the same topology key to prevent drift.

Day-2 operations: node add/replace flows:
1) Add node: terraform apply -> create VM or trigger BMC -> cloud-init registers node -> k8s labels applied -> optionally join to node pool autoscaler.
2) Replace node (failed hardware): stop scheduling, cordon node, drain gracefully with chosen grace period, remove from TF state (if baremetal) or mark for reclamation (vSphere).
3) Rebalance: when adding nodes across racks, use a short rolling drain of low-priority workloads with batch size = floor(total_replicas / 10) to limit churn.

Upgrade plan (control plane and workers) — conservative strategy:
- Pre-checks (automated): node readiness %, pending pods, eviction pressure, PV attachments, CSI driver versions.
- Canary window: pick a single node in rack-A, drain, upgrade kubelet/containerd/kernel, rejoin, run smoke tests against local services for 10 minutes.
- Rollout phases:
  * Phase 0: control-plane single master in maintenance, etcd quorum check, snapshot etcd, run sanity.
  * Phase 1: worker canaries (1 per rack) — validate networking and storage + app-level smoke tests.
  * Phase 2: bulk workers with rack-aware rolling (parallelism = 2 racks * N where N = min(3, floor(nodes_per_rack/10))).
  * Phase 3: cleanup and revert window close.
- Rollback: maintain a documented reprovision path + quick reprovision Terraform plan for previous image/kubelet version; if majority of racks fail, automate redeploy to previous known-good state.

Observability hooks to include in module outputs:
- Prometheus scrape targets for node-exporter, kubelet/readiness, and BMC-provision metrics.
- A slack/webhook post for each terraform apply that changes > 5 nodes or touches control-plane.
- Terraform plan diffs as artifact stored in S3 (or internal blobstore) for audit.

Checklist for a single upgrade wave (operator-oriented):
- [ ] Confirm etcd snapshot success + upload path verified
- [ ] No pending K8s jobs older than 2h
- [ ] CSI driver compatible versions present in CRDs
- [ ] Canary smoke tests defined and runnable (curl + synthetic transactions)
- [ ] Cluster autoscaler disabled for duration of bulk node operations
- [ ] Maintenance windows respected per customer SLA (documented in module)

Terraform implementation notes / gotchas:
- State sharding: keep vSphere VM resources in a separate state backend from baremetal BMC resources to reduce lock contention during Day-2 partial operations.
- Use lifecycle { ignore_changes = [labels, annotations] } in node resources that are managed by K8s controllers to avoid churn between Terraform and K8s.
- Use null_resource local-exec hooks sparingly; prefer sidecar operator that takes desired topology as CRD so Terraform only manages infra and operator drives node labeling/join.
- Avoid trying to code strong anti-affinity in infra layer for vSphere; instead, surface placement hints and let scheduler or external placement operator reconcile final pod placement.

Safety & Rollback playbook (quick):
- If >20% nodes in a rack go NotReady during a wave, pause rollout and trigger node-repair playbook: 1) mark nodes unschedulable, 2) attempt kubelet restart via systemd, 3) reprovision if hardware fault found, 4) if failure persists, re-add previous image via reprovision plan.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Do we want a small placement operator that consumes Terraform-generated placement tags and creates K8s NodeAffinity CRs for critical workloads? Pros: stronger guarantees; Cons: more moving parts during bootstrap.
- Treatment of PV topology when using legacy storage backends — need mapping between PV storage-affinity and node rack labels.
- How to represent multi-tenant racks where hardware ownership and maintenance windows differ.

Notes-to-self / short-term next steps:
- Draft a CRD for "placement-hint" that canonicalizes topology keys between infra modules and K8s scheduling resources.
- Prototype state sharding layout: one backend per site_zone + one backend per vcenter-cluster.
- Run a dry-run on staging: create 6 nodes across 3 racks, deploy a 5-replica stateful app, validate anti-affinity distribution.

References and links:
- Confluence: private-deploy/day2-affinity (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-1423 (upgrade window epic)
- Early prototype PR: github:infra/terraform-modules/pull/98

This file is a sketch — expect many TODOs and divergence once hardware constraints from customer X are known. Keep focused on core primitives: 1) consistent topology labels, 2) light-weight placement hints from infra, 3) conservative, observable upgrade waves.
